ribbon.title: Painted ribbon
ribbon.text: A fan of moving averages behind the candles. The band paints green while buyers are in control and red while sellers are — flips in color are where trends turn.

candles.title: Colored candles
candles.text: Green or red when a real trend is underway, yellow when there isn’t one.

tp.title: TP
tp.text: Marks where a past Buy or Sell would have closed in profit.

buySell.title: BUY / SELL
buySell.text: Fires only when most of the 7 checks agree and the bigger-picture trend points the same way. On charts under 4h the new trend must also hold for 3 candles with solid strength. A ✓ marks past signals that ended in profit.

invalidation.title: Invalidation zone
invalidation.text: The glowing band and dashed line show where the latest signal would be proven wrong, tagged with its Δ Volume.

spikes.title: ⚡ Spikes
spikes.text: Sudden, news-like candles. Signals that bet against a fresh spike are skipped for a few candles.

events.title: Event countdown
events.text: Big scheduled US releases — Fed decisions, CPI, jobs, GDP — show up to a day ahead. Signals pause from 30 minutes before until an hour after each one.

sideways.title: Sideways tag + range box
sideways.text: When price drifts in a range, a grey box marks its ceiling and floor. Trend signals hold off on charts under 4h; from 1h up, range mode adds R·BUY near the floor and R·SELL near the ceiling until price breaks out.

thin.title: Thin market tag
thin.text: Shows when too little is trading for reliable signals. BUY/SELL switch off until volume returns.

signals15m.title: “Signals: 15m” tag
signals15m.text: On 1m and 5m charts, signals come from the 15m chart and are placed on yours, so you get 15m direction with short-chart timing.

confirm.title: Confirm before you enter
confirm.text: Glance at the Signal check verdict first. When most checks point one way, think twice before taking the other side.

stop.title: Set your stop with a reason
stop.text: The dashed invalidation line marks where the signal stops making sense. It’s a ready-made stop level, and the gap to it tells you how big a position to take.

trend.title: See the trend instantly
trend.text: Colored candles show a market that’s moving with purpose. A chart full of grey is a market without direction — often a good time to wait.

stretched.title: Catch stretched moves
stretched.text: A strong trend with RSI or Stochastic at an extreme may be running out of steam. Late entries there carry extra risk.

money.title: Follow the real money
money.text: Δ Volume uses actual market buys and sells from the exchange. A signal backed by heavy one-sided volume is stronger than one without it.

track.title: Check the track record
track.text: Before trusting a signal, look at how this chart’s past ones did — not just how often they won, but average win vs. loss and the result per trade after fees.

winners.title: Let winners run
winners.text: From 15m up, the track record trails your stop behind the price and exits when the trend turns. Expect fewer wins but much bigger ones — cutting winners early is what hurts most.

tiny.title: Tiny moves on 1m–5m
tiny.text: Short candles move less than fees, so these charts borrow the 15m chart’s signals. You get 15m direction with short-chart timing.

choppy.title: Choppy ranges
choppy.text: Trend signals step aside when price goes sideways. From 1h up, range mode trades bounces off the box edges instead; below 1h it marks the box and waits for a breakout.

news.title: Scheduled news
news.text: Fed decisions, CPI, jobs and GDP are flagged up to a day ahead, and signals pause from 30 minutes before to an hour after.

shocks.title: Sudden shocks
shocks.text: Outsized candles are marked ⚡, and signals that bet against a fresh shock are skipped.

thin.title: Thin markets
thin.text: When too little is trading, signals switch off instead of guessing.

headlines.title: Surprise headlines
headlines.text: Unscheduled news can’t be seen coming on any chart — size positions for the unexpected.

past.title: Past ≠ future
past.text: Track records come from this chart’s recent history. Markets change, and small samples can flatter or mislead.

workflow.s1: Take your direction from the 4h or daily chart.
workflow.s2: Act on signals from 15m up; on 1m–5m they’re the 15m signals, so use the short chart to time your entry.
workflow.s3: Place your stop at the invalidation line, then trail it as price moves your way.
workflow.s4: Check the track record pays off after fees.
workflow.s5: Try the setup in Paper Trading first.
